name: Group f/64
summary: Sharp, rich black-and-white contact prints of rocks, plants, shells and faces, made on large cameras at the smallest stop. The group named itself after that stop.

philosophy.core_thesis: Pure photography needs no borrowed look from painting; the large camera, the small stop and the full tonal scale are enough.
design_principles: Use an 8×10 in view camera and a lens of 210mm to 300mm, stopped down to f/45 to f/64.
Expose for the shadows and develop for the highlights: place the darkest detail on Zone III and the brightest on Zone VII or VIII.
Make a contact print on glossy paper (grade 2) with no enlargement, so that the print is as sharp as the negative.
Show the whole scale: a pure black in the deepest shadow and a clean white in the highest light, with 9 or 10 zones between.
Take the subject as it is: a rock, a pepper, a dune or a face, framed by the shape of the plate.
Mount the print on white board with no frame decoration.
anti_patterns: Soft focus, gum or bromoil handwork
Retouching the negative to change the scene
Cropping a print to repair the framing

composition.framing: Full plate, exact; the edge of the 8×10 negative is the edge of the print.
composition.viewpoint: Low tripod, 0.5m to 5m from the subject; the camera is level with the form.
composition.geometry: Curves, ripples and ridges; one strong form against a quiet ground.
composition.subject_placement: Centred or on a third; the main form fills 60–90% of the plate.

principles.rule: Let 1 primary form fill 60–90% of the plate; a second form takes under 15%.
Hold 3 planes sharp at f/64: near 0.5m, middle 5m and far to infinity.
Print 9 to 10 zones, from pure black at Zone 0 to paper white at Zone X.
Keep the 4:5 ratio of the 8×10 plate, with no crop.
Repeat a ripple, a scale or a leaf at an interval of 1/8 to 1/12 of the plate width.

light.quality: Clear, hard-edged light with deep, detailed shadows.
light.direction: Side light at 45° to 90° to bring out texture; backlight for leaves.
light.time_of_day: Early morning or late afternoon; midday for shells and studio work

lens_and_camera.focus: Tilt the back and focus on a third of the way into the scene; the depth of field covers 0.5m to infinity at f/64.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Neutral black and white with a full scale and no toning.
grade_recipe: Convert to monochrome with a neutral mix (R 30, G 59, B 11).
Set the black point at 0% and the white point at 99%.
Apply a −1 contraction on a flat scene or an expansion of +1 on a flat day, as for N−1 and N+1 development.
Dodge Zone III shadows by +0.3 stop and burn skies by −0.5 stop.
Add no grain and no vignette.
colour_and_grade.grain: None: fine detail at 8×10 contact scale

subject_and_staging.staging: Minimal. The maker picks the form, the hour and the stop, and removes nothing from the scene.
subject_and_staging.direction: Sit a portrait in open shade for 2s to 4s; the sitter holds still.

workflow: Place shadows on Zone III by spot meter, and set the highlight zone by the time of development.
Develop each sheet by its own time (N−1, N, N+1).
Contact print on glossy paper at grade 2 with a printing frame.
Mount on white board; sign and date below the print.
post_processing.output: A glossy contact print 8×10 in (20×25cm), mounted on white board.

emotion.target_response: Awe at exact detail: the viewer feels a rock or a leaf as a structure that has no equal.

use_cases: image prompts for monumental sharp scenes
avoid_when: The brief needs soft mood, motion or a candid moment.
The camera is small and handheld; the f/64 numbers do not apply.

modifiers.how: Move to a 9×12cm plate and a 150mm lens, a plain grey ground and a frontal view; photograph 20 or more of one kind.
Switch to a soft-focus lens at f/5.6, a platinum print and a mist of 40–60%; keep one subject.

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 210 to 300 mm on 8×10 in.

aspect_ratio.note: The 8×10 in contact plate is the frame.

sources.title: Mary Street Alinder, Ansel Adams: A Biography (Henry Holt, 1996)
